title: Sugreeva kills Mahodara
introduction: Ravana sends Mahodara to the battle-field. Mahodara creates havoc, by cutting off the hands, feet and thighs of monkeys. Some monkeys seek refuge with Sugreeva and some ran away for life. Sugreeva attacks Mahodara and initially kills the horses of the latter. Both of them fight till the weapons in their hands get broken. Then, they start wrestling with each other, till they get exhausted. Finally, Sugreeva cuts off Mahodara's head with a huge sword.
closing: Thus, this is the 97th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
हन्यमाने बले तूर्णमन्योन्यन् ते महामृधे |
सरसीव महाघर्मे सूपक्षीणे बभूवतुः
verses.iast:
hanyamAne bale tUrṇamanyonyan te mahAmṛdhe |
sarasIva mahAgharme sUpakṣIṇe babhUvatuḥ
verses.translation: Being killed by each other in that major battle, those two armies were very much diminished soon, like two lakes in a severe summer.

verses.devanagari:
स्वबलस्य विघातेन विरूपाक्षवधेन च |
बभूव द्विगुणन् क्रुद्धो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
verses.iast:
svabalasya vighAtena virUpAkṣavadhena ca |
babhUva dviguṇan kruddho rAvaṇo rAkṣasAdhipaḥ
verses.translation: Ravana the lord of demons got doubly enraged because of the destroyal of his own army and the fall of Virupaksha.

verses.devanagari:
प्रक्षीणन् तु बलं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानन् वलीमुखैः |
बभूवास्य व्यथा युद्धे प्रेक्ष्य दैवविपर्ययम्
verses.iast:
prakṣIṇan tu balaṃ dṛṣṭvA vadhyamAnan valImukhaiḥ |
babhUvAsya vyathA yuddhe prekṣya daivaviparyayam
verses.translation: He felt restless to find his own army diminished while being killed by the monkeys and to see the reversal of his fate.

verses.devanagari:
उवाच च समीपस्थं महोदरमरिन्दमम् |
अस्मिन्काले महाबाहो जयाशा त्वयि मे स्थिता
verses.iast:
uvAca ca samIpasthaṃ mahodaramarindamam |
asminkAle mahAbAho jayAśA tvayi me sthitA
verses.translation: He spoke to Mahodara, the annihilator of enemies, standing beside him (as follows): "O the long-armed! At this juncture, my hope for victory is centered in you."

glosses.meaning: who was standing nearby (as follows): mahaabaaho = O the long armed!

verses.devanagari:
जहि शत्रुचमून् वीर दर्शयाद्य पराक्रमम् |
भर्तृपिण्डस्य कालोअयं निर्वेष्टुन् साधु युध्यताम्
verses.iast:
jahi śatrucamUn vIra darśayAdya parAkramam |
bhartṛpiṇḍasya kAloayaṃ nirveṣṭun sAdhu yudhyatAm
verses.translation: "O the brave demon! Destroy the army of our enemies. Show your prowess now. This is the time to repay the debt of your master (received in the form of sustenance from him). Fight well."

glosses.meaning: of your master (in the form of subsistence received from him)

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा राक्षसेन्द्रं महोदरः |
प्रविवेशारिसेनान् स पतङ्ग इव पावकम्
verses.iast:
evamuktastathetyuktvA rAkṣasendraṃ mahodaraḥ |
praviveśArisenAn sa patañga iva pAvakam
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Ravana, Mahodara the chief of demons saying "So it be", penetrated into the army of enemies, as a moth rushed into a flame.

verses.devanagari:
ततः स कदनन् चक्रे वानराणां महाबलः |
भर्तृवाक्येन तेजस्वी स्वेन वीर्येण चोदितः
verses.iast:
tataḥ sa kadanan cakre vAnarAṇAṃ mahAbalaḥ |
bhartṛvAkyena tejasvI svena vIryeṇa coditaḥ
verses.translation: Emboldened by the words of his master, that mighty demon, with full of energy, destroyed the monkeys by dint of his own valour.

glosses.meaning: by the words of ihs master
by dint of his own valour.

verses.devanagari:
वानराश्च महासत्त्वः प्रगृह्य विपुलाः शिलाः |
प्रविश्यारिबलं भीमं जघ्नस्ते सर्वराक्षसान्
verses.iast:
vānarāśca mahāsattvaḥ pragṛhya vipulāḥ śilāḥ |
praviśyāribalaṃ bhīmaṃ jaghnaste sarvarākṣasān
verses.translation: Taking hold of huge rocks and penetrating the terrific army of enemies, those highly strong monkeys too started killing all the demons.

glosses.meaning: taking hold of vipulaaH shilaaH = huge rocks

verses.devanagari:
महोदरः सुसंक्रुद्धः शरैः काज्ञ्चनभूषणैः |
चिच्चेद पाणिपादोरु वानराणां महाहवे
verses.iast:
mahodaraḥ susaṅkruddhaḥ śaraiḥ kājJṇcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ |
cicceda pāṇipādoru vānarāṇāṃ mahāhave
verses.translation: In that great battle, the highly enraged Mahodara, with his arrows decked in gold, chopped off the hands, feet and thighs of monkeys.

verses.devanagari:
ततस्ते वानराः सर्वे राक्षसैरर्दिता भृशम् |
दिशो दश द्रुताः केचित्केचित्सुग्रीवमाश्रिताः
verses.iast:
tataste vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasairarditā bhṛśam |
diśo daśa drutāḥ kecitkecitsugrīvamāśritāḥ
verses.translation: Then, among all those monkeys who were tormented by the demons, some ran away into ten directions. Some others sought refuge with Sugreeva.

verses.devanagari:
प्रभग्नान् समरे दृष्ट्वा वानराणां महाचमूम् |
अभिदुद्राव सुग्रीवो महोदरमनन्तरम्
verses.iast:
prabhagnAn samare dṛṣṭvA vAnarAṇAṃ mahAcamUm |
abhidudrAva sugrIvo mahodaramanantaram
verses.translation: Seeing the large army of monkeys defeated in the battle, Sugreeva rushed towards Mahodara who was immediately close to him.

glosses.meaning: who was immediately close to him.

verses.devanagari:
प्रगृह्य विपुलान् घोरां महीधर समान् शिलाम् |
चिक्षेप च महातेजास्तद्वधाय हरीश्वरः
verses.iast:
pragṛhya vipulAn ghorAṃ mahIdhara samAn śilAm |
cikṣepa ca mahAtejAstadvadhAya harIśvaraḥ
verses.translation: Seizing hold of a large and terrific rock, which looked like a mountain, Sugreeva who was endowed with a great energy, hurled it with an aim to kill the demon.

glosses.meaning: and equal in size to a mountain
who was endowed with a great energy

verses.devanagari:
तामापतन्तीन् सहसा शिलान् दृष्ट्वा महोदरः |
असम्भ्रान्तस्ततो बाणैर्निर्बिभेद दुरासदाम्
verses.iast:
tAmApatantIn sahasA śilAn dṛṣṭvA mahodaraḥ |
asambhrAntastato bAṇairnirbibheda durAsadAm
verses.translation: Seeing that rock falling suddenly, Mahodara, then unagitated, tore it with his arrows, though it was difficult to approach.

glosses.meaning: though it was difficult to approach.

verses.devanagari:
रक्षसा तेन बाणौघैर्निकृत्ता सा सहस्रधा |
निपपात शिलाभूमौ गृध्रचक्रमिवाकुलम्
verses.iast:
rakṣasA tena bAṇaughairnikṛttA sA sahasradhA |
nipapAta śilAbhUmau gṛdhracakramivAkulam
verses.translation: That rock, broken to a thousand pieces by that demon with a multitude of his arrows, forthwith fell down on earth, like a flock of frightened vultures.

glosses.meaning: with a multitude of his arrows
like a flock of frightened vultures.

verses.devanagari:
तान् तु भिन्नान् शिलां दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवः क्रोधमूर्छितः |
सालमुत्पाट्य चिक्षेप रक्षसे रणमूर्धनि
verses.iast:
tAn tu bhinnAn śilAṃ dṛṣṭvA sugrIvaḥ krodhamUrchitaḥ |
sAlamutpAṭya cikṣepa rakṣase raṇamUrdhani
verses.translation: Filled with rage on seeing that rock broken and uprooting a Sala tree, Sugreeva hurled it at his enemy and Mahodara chopped it off into many pieces.

glosses.meaning: chopped it off naikadhaa = into many pieces.

verses.devanagari:
शरैश्च विददारैनन् शूरः परपुरञ्जयः |
स ददर्श ततः क्रुद्धः परिघं पतितं भुवि
verses.iast:
śaraiśca vidadArainan śUraḥ parapurañjayaḥ |
sa dadarśa tataḥ kruddhaḥ parighaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi
verses.translation: The valiant Mahodara, who was the tormentator of hostile forces, lacerated Sugreeva with his arrows. That enraged Sugreeva then saw an iron rod on the ground.

verses.devanagari:
आविध्य तु स तन् दीप्तं परिघं तस्य दर्शयन् |
परिघाग्रेण वेगेन जघानास्य हयोत्तमान्
verses.iast:
Avidhya tu sa tan dIptaṃ parighaṃ tasya darśayan |
parighAgreṇa vegena jaghAnAsya hayottamAn
verses.translation: Swinging that flashing iron rod and showing it to him, Sugreeva killed the excellent horses of Mahodara with that iron rod of terrible speed.

verses.devanagari:
तस्माद्धतहयाद्वीरः सोअवप्लुत्य महारथात् |
गदान् जग्राह सङ्क्रुद्धो राक्षसोअथ महोदरः
verses.iast:
tasmAddhatahayAdvIraḥ soavaplutya mahArathAt |
gadAn jagrAha sañkruddho rAkṣasoatha mahodaraḥ
verses.translation: Jumping down from that huge chariot, whose horses had been killed, that valiant Mahodara the demon, thereupon seized hold of a mace with anger.

verses.devanagari:
गदापरिघहस्तौ तौ युधि वीरौ समीयतुः |
नर्दन्तौ गोवृषप्रख्यौ घनाविव सविद्युतौ
verses.iast:
gadAparighahastau tau yudhi vIrau samIyatuḥ |
nardantau govṛṣaprakhyau ghanAviva savidyutau
verses.translation: With a mace and an iron road respectively in their hands and roaring like two bulls and resembling like two clouds charged with lightning, those two heroes closed in for a battle.

glosses.meaning: with a mace and an iron hand respectively in their hands

verses.devanagari:
ततः क्रुद्धो गदां तस्य चिक्षेप रजनीचरः |
ज्वलन्तीं भास्कराभासां सुग्रीवाय महोदरः
verses.iast:
tataḥ kruddho gadāṃ tasya cikṣepa rajanīcaraḥ |
jvalantīṃ bhāskarābhāsāṃ sugrīvāya mahodaraḥ
verses.translation: Mahodara the demon was angry with Sgureeva and thereupon hurled his blazing mace, which shone like the sun, on Sugreeva.

verses.devanagari:
गदां तां सुमहाघोरामापतन्तीं महाबलः |
सुग्रीवो रोषताम्राक्षः समुद्यम्य महाहवे
आजघान गदान् तस्य परिघेण हरीश्वरः |
पपात स गदोद्भिन्नः परिघस्तस्य भूतले
verses.iast:
gadāṃ tāṃ sumahāghorāmāpatantīṃ mahābalaḥ |
sugrīvo roṣatāmrākṣaḥ samudyamya mahāhave
AjaghAna gadAn tasya parigheṇa harIśvaraḥ |
papAta sa gadodbhinnaḥ parighastasya bhUtale
verses.translation: Seeing that highly terrible mace, falling on him in that great battle, the mighty Sugreeva, the King of monkeys, was enraged with red eyes and struck that mace, by lifting up the iron rod. That iron rod broke off and fell on the ground.

verses.devanagari:
ततो जग्राह तेजस्वी सुग्रीवो वसुधातलात् |
आयसं मुसलन् घोरन् सर्वतो हेमभूषितम्
verses.iast:
tato jagrAha tejasvI sugrIvo vasudhAtalAt |
Ayasaṃ musalan ghoran sarvato hemabhUṣitam
verses.translation: Thereupon, the spirited Sugreeva took hold of a formidable steel club, entirely decked with gold, from the earth-surface.

verses.devanagari:
स तमुद्यम्य चिक्षेप सोऽप्यस्य प्राक्षिपद्गदाम् |
भिन्नावन्योन्यमासाद्य पेततुस्तौ महीतले
verses.iast:
sa tamudyamya cikṣepa so'pyasya prākṣipadgadām |
bhinnAvanyonyamAsAdya petatustau mahītale
verses.translation: Lifting that steel club, Sugreeva hurled it. Mahodara too hurled another mace on him. Those two weapons, clashing each other, broke and fell on the floor.

verses.devanagari:
ततो भिन्नप्रहरणौ मुष्टिभ्यान् तौ समीयतुः |
तेजो बलसमाविष्टौ दीप्ताविव हुताशनौ
verses.iast:
tato bhinnapraharaṇau muṣṭibhyān tau samīyatuḥ |
tejo balasamAviṣṭau dIptAviva hutAśanau
verses.translation: As all their weapons were broken, those two warriors, who were endowed with spirit and strength, resembling two blazing fires, started contending with fists.

glosses.meaning: who were endowed with spirit and strength

verses.devanagari:
जघ्नतुस्तौ तदान्योन्यं नेदतुश्च पुनः पुनः |
तलैश्चान्योन्यमाहत्य पेततुर्धरणीतले
verses.iast:
jaghnatustau tadAnyonyaṃ nedatuśca punaḥ punaḥ |
talaiścAnyonyamAhatya petaturdharaṇItale
verses.translation: Roaring again and again, those two warriors then banged each other. Slapping each other with their palms, they rolled on the earth's surface.

verses.devanagari:
उत्पेततुस्ततस्तूर्णन् जघ्नतुश् च परस्परम् |
भुजैश्चिक्षेपतुर्वीरावन्योन्यमपराजितौ
verses.iast:
utpetatustatastUrṇan jaghnatuś ca parasparam |
bhujaiścikṣepaturvIrAvanyonyamaparAjitau
verses.translation: They raised quickly on their feet and then began to strike each other. Remaining unyielded, the two heroes pushed each other on their shoulders.

verses.devanagari:
जग्मुतुस्तौ श्रमं वीरौ बाहुयुद्धे पांतपौ |
जहार च तदा खग्डमदूरपरिवर्तिनम्
राक्षसश्चर्मणा सार्धं महावेगो महोदरः |
verses.iast:
jagmutustau śramaṃ vīrau bāhuyuddhe pāntapau |
jahāra ca tadā khagḍamadūraparivartinam
rākṣasaścarmaṇā sArdhaṃ mahAvego mahodaraḥ |
verses.translation: Those two heroes, the annihilators their enemies, felt exhausted in the course of their wrestling. Then the highly fast Mahodara the demon took hold of a sword and a shield, lying not very far.

glosses.meaning: in the course of their wrestling

verses.devanagari:
तथैव च महाखड्गन् चर्मणा पतितन् सह
जग्राह वानरश्रेष्ठः सुग्रीवो वेगवत्तरः |
verses.iast:
tathaiva ca mahAkhaḍgan carmaṇA patitan saha
jagrAha vAnaraśreṣṭhaḥ sugrIvo vegavattaraḥ |
verses.translation: In the same way, the highly swift Sugreeva the foremost of monkeys took hold of a large sword together with a shield, lying there.

verses.devanagari:
तौ तु रोषपरीताङ्गौ नर्दन्तावभ्यधावताम्
उद्यतासी रणे हृष्टौ युधि शस्त्रविशारदौ |
verses.iast:
tau tu roṣaparItAñgau nardantAvabhyadhAvatAm
udyatAsI raṇe hṛṣṭau yudhi śastraviśAradau |
verses.translation: Thereupon, those two warriors, who were skilled in the use of weaponry in the battle-field and whose limbs were seized with anger, galloped forward, roaring with joy, with their swords upraised.

glosses.meaning: who were skilled in the use of weaponry
and whose limbs were seized with aner

verses.devanagari:
दक्षिणं मण्डलन् चोभौ तौ तूर्णन् सम्परीयतुः
अन्योन्यमभिसङ्क्रुद्धौ जये प्रणिहितावुभौ |
verses.iast:
dakṣiṇaṃ maṇḍalan cobhau tau tUrṇan samparIyatuḥ
anyonyamabhisañkruddhau jaye praṇihitAvubhau |
verses.translation: With their thoughts concentrated on one point of victory, both the warriors were enraged with each other and performed circumambulations form left to right, very quickly.

glosses.meaning: with their thoughts concentrated on one point

verses.devanagari:
स तु शूरो महावेगो वीर्यश्लाघी महोदरः
महाचर्मणि तन् खड्गं पातयामास दुर्मतिः |
verses.iast:
sa tu śUro mahAvego vIryaślAghI mahodaraḥ
mahAcarmaṇi tan khaḍgaṃ pAtayAmAsa durmatiḥ |
verses.translation: That valiant and evil-minded Mahodara, who was boasting of his own prowess, let fall with very high speed, that sword on the heavy shield of Sugreeva.

glosses.meaning: who was boasting of his own prowess

verses.devanagari:
लग्नमुत्कर्षतः खड्गन् खड्गेन कपिकुञ्जरः
जहार सशिरस्त्राणन् कुण्डलोपहितन् शिरः |
verses.iast:
lagnamutkarṣataḥ khaḍgan khaḍgena kapikuñjaraḥ
jahAra saśirastrAṇan kuṇḍalopahitan śiraḥ |
verses.translation: Even while Mahodara was extracting his sword which had got struck in the shield, Sugreeva severed with his own sword, Mahodara's head, which was adorned with ear-rings and helmet.

glosses.meaning: which had got struck in the shield

verses.devanagari:
निकृत्तशिरसस्तस्य पतितस्य महीतले
तद्बलन् राक्षसेन्द्रस्य दृष्ट्वा तत्र न तिष्ठति |
verses.iast:
nikṛttaśirasastasya patitasya mahItale
tadbalan rAkṣasendrasya dṛṣṭvA tatra na tiṣṭhati |
verses.translation: While Mahodara, with his head chopped off, was falling on the ground, Ravana's army, on seeing it, could no longer be seen on the battle-field.

verses.devanagari:
हत्वा तन् वानरैः सार्धं ननाद मुदितो हरिः
चुक्रोध च दशग्रीवो बभौ हृष्टश्च राघवः |
verses.iast:
hatvA tan vAnaraiḥ sArdhaṃ nanAda mudito hariḥ
cukrodha ca daśagrIvo babhau hṛṣṭaśca rAghavaḥ |
verses.translation: Having killed Mahodara, Sugreeva made a rejoicing roar with his monkeys. Ravana was enraged. Rama looked rejoicing.

verses.devanagari:
विषण्णवदनाः सर्वे राक्षसा दीनचेतसः
विद्रवन्ति ततः सर्वे भयवित्रस्तचेतसः |
verses.iast:
viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve rākṣasā dīnacetasaḥ
vidravanti tataḥ sarve bhayavitrastacetasaḥ |
verses.translation: With their faces looking low-spirited all the demons felt dejected. With their minds stricken with fear, all of them ran away from the battle-field.

glosses.meaning: with their minds stricken with fear

verses.devanagari:
महोदरं तं विनिपात्य भूमौ |
महागिरेः कीर्णमिवैकदेशम् |
सूर्यात्मजस्तत्र रराज लक्ष्म्या |
सूर्यः स्वतेजोभिरिवाप्रधृष्यः
verses.iast:
mahodaraṃ taṃ vinipātya bhūmau |
mahāgireḥ kīrṇamivaikadeśam |
sūryātmajastatra rarāja lakṣmyā |
sūryaḥ svatejobhirivāpradhṛṣyaḥ
verses.translation: Having thrown down to the ground that Mahodara, looking like a part of a huge mountain lying shattered the invincible Sugreeva shone in glory in the battle-field like the sun shines with its rays.

verses.devanagari:
अथ विजयमवाप्य वानरेन्द्रः |
समरमुखे सुरसिद्धयक्षसंघैः |
अवनितलगतैश्च भूतसंघै |
र्हरुषसमाकुलितैर्निरीक्ष्यमाणः
verses.iast:
atha vijayamavāpya vānarendraḥ |
samaramukhe surasiddhayakṣasaṅghaiḥ |
avanitalagataiśca bhūtasaṅghai |
rharuṣasamākulitairnirīkṣyamāṇaḥ
verses.translation: Having attained victory in the battle-front, Sugreeva then continued to be looked at by the multitude of gods, Siddhas (a class of demigods who are endowed with mystic powers) and Yakshas (another class of demigods attending on Kubera, the god of riches) as also a host of beings standing on the earth's surface who were all overwhelmed with joy.

glosses.itrans: the god of riches) bhuutasamghaiH cha
glosses.iast: the god of rices) bhūtasamghaiḥ ca
glosses.devanagari: थे गोद् ओf रिचेस्) भूतसम्घैः च
glosses.meaning: as also a multitude of beings
who were all overwhelmed with joy.
